en.html:
A bold design, certainly. With practically empty hands, they proposed to challenge an enormous military regime and change its very nature.

How much chance did it have? I could not say. But suppose we did nothing and watched. When the moment suited them, the occupation forces would remove Rokuhara—and either succeed, bringing all Yamato under occupation,

or lose, leaving Rokuhara the country's sole ruler. One of those futures awaited us. After savage fighting.

No, I was forgetting a third. Neither side might settle matters. The war could simply go on and on. There was our worst possibility.

If we wanted to refuse those futures and obtain even a <ruby>comparatively<rt>・・・</rt></ruby> decent one, some action was necessary. Call the Prince and the Chief's plan reckless, and it was reckless. Call it reasonable, and that also was difficult to deny.

ja.html:
雄略と呼ぶべきだろう。
　徒手空拳に等しい身で強大な軍事政権に挑み、その
体質を改めさせようというのであるから。

　成就する見込みの程は知れない。
　が、何もせず情況を見守れば、進駐軍は時節が到来
次第六波羅の排除に乗り出し――これを遂げて大和を
完全な占領下に置くか。

　それとも六波羅が勝利を得て大和唯一の支配権者と
なりおおせるか。
　この国はどちらかの結末を迎えるだろう。……苛烈
な交戦の後に。

　いや、可能性はもう一つある。
　両者の相克に決着がつかず、延々と戦争が続く――
という最悪の展開も起こり得る。

　喜ばしからざる運命を拒否し、<ruby>比較的<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>にでも良好な
未来を手に入れたいと望むなら、やはり行動は必要だ。
　親王と署長、この二人の構想は、暴挙といえば暴挙
であったが至当といえば至当に違いなかった。

This plan could save Yamato. Believing that required no great effort.

It would not be easy. There would be discrepancies, oversights, difficulties enough. Still, the Prince made one feel that he might manage it. And he had the Chief beside him.

More to the point, had I produced a better plan myself? I had not. On what grounds, then, was I entitled to dismiss his?

From no direction could I call the Prince wrong.

...Very well. Could I do it?

Attack Moriuji Ashikaga and take his life?

en.html: To save many good people, kill one evil man. ............That was what I had done already. Again and again and again. To stop the spread of Silver Starcalamity, I had cut down any number of warriors parasitized by her “eggs.” Remove one evil. Preserve many good. Exactly the same. Not one difference anywhere. Both were,◆ —nothing but self-righteousness. For the country. For the people... Peel away that fine-sounding exteriorskin, and the actual shape showed underneath. I was not proposing anything so foolish as to suspect the Prince of secretly pursuing his own profit. But once we chose to crush our opponent through violence, the motive did not change the nature of the act. Self-righteousness remained self-righteousness. For my good, I called his good evil, and buried it. One sword, one killing—thus are good and evil balancedOne blade, one death: good and evil offset. My answer was decided.

ja.text:
多くの善き人々を救うために、
　一人の悪しき者を殺す。

　…………それは、

　俺が既に幾度も、幾度も、繰り返してきた所業だ。

　銀星号わざわいの拡大を阻止すべく、
〝卵〟に寄生された武者を幾人となく斬り殺した。

　一悪を断ち多善を残す。

　まるで同じだ。
　何処にも違いなど無い。

　どちらも、◆

　――――独善に過ぎない。

　国のため。人のため……
　そんな聞こえの良い外面かわを一枚剥けば、そこに真実
の姿が覗く。

　親王の動機が実は私利私欲だとか、間の抜けた事を
言うつもりはない。
　しかし、対立者を暴力で挫くという道を選ぶのなら、
動機がどうあれそれはやはり独善の行いなのだ。

　我の善のため、
　彼の善を悪と称して葬る。

　一剣一殺是善悪相殺いっけんいっさつこれぜんあくそうさい。

　俺の返答は定まった。

en.html:
And while thinking that, could I kill Moriuji Ashikaga without objection?

They were both human.
Both <ruby>ordinary men<rt>ordinary people</rt></ruby>, with good and evil, achievements and sins.

From where I stood, the Chief's good was prominent and Moriuji's evil was prominent. That was all. A man standing elsewhere would see something else.

Yet I would call one evil and kill him; call the other good and let him live.

—Self-righteousness.

Muramasa had said it. Self-righteousness was the root of conflict. It justified killing, and made the killing continue without end.

Yes.
That much, she was right about.

そう思う一方、足利護氏は構わず斬れるのか。

　同じ人間である。
　善あり悪あり功あり罪ある、同じ<ruby>只人<rt>ただびと</rt></ruby>である。

　単に俺の立つ位置からは署長の善ばかりが、護氏の
悪ばかりが目立つというだけに過ぎない。
　異なる位置に立つ者には、異なる見方があるだろう。

　なのに一方のみ悪として斬り、もう一方を善として
生かすのは、

　――独善である。

　村正は言った。
　独善こそ争いの根源。殺し合いを正当化し、際限も
なく続けさせる元凶――と。

　そう。
　それは、その通りなのだ。
